basis: Christ as the way to the Father
note: Augustine reads Jesus’s “I am the way” as Christ himself mediating access to the Father; this interprets the route-and-destination relation as a person rather than a road.

basis: two ways of life and death
note: The teaching opens by distinguishing a way of life from a way of death; it places the commentary’s contrast between the guided path and its opposite in early Christian moral instruction.

basis: the way of life and the way of death
note: The Didache's opening two-ways instruction turns path language into a catechetical division between life and death, a compact Christian interpretive frame for the single way and its opposed courses.

basis: two ways of light and darkness
note: Barnabas describes two ways, light and darkness, under different authorities; this makes the competing routes a community’s ethical and spiritual allegiance.

basis: walker in darkness does not know where going
note: The person who walks in darkness cannot know the destination because darkness blinds the eyes, a direct cognitive and spatial rendering of being lost.

basis: walk as the exemplar walked
note: The one who remains in Christ is obliged to walk as he walked, making a prior walk an exemplary track for later followers.

basis: straying sheep return to their shepherd
note: The readers were straying like sheep and have now returned to the shepherd and guardian; the route from loss to restored guidance is explicit.

basis: straying sheep returned to shepherd and overseer
note: The audience was straying like sheep but has returned to the shepherd and overseer of souls, combining lostness, return, and a restoring guide.

basis: walk worthy toward God's kingdom and glory
note: Paul urges conduct worthy of the God who calls believers into kingdom and glory, joining a moral walk to a destination beyond the journey.

basis: God directs a journey's way
note: Paul asks God and the Lord Jesus to direct his way to the recipients, a specific travel prayer that supplies a less developed but concrete guide-to-destination parallel.

basis: the serpent leads minds away from devotion
note: Paul fears that, as the serpent deceived Eve, the community’s minds may be led astray from devotion to Christ; this gives the commentary’s ambushing adversary a specific Christian counterpart.

basis: judgment accounts for deeds done in life
note: All appear before the judgment seat to receive for what they did in the body, connecting the commentary’s Day of Reckoning with a person’s lived course.

basis: love is walking according to commandments
note: The epistle defines love as walking according to God's commandments, directly coupling the commentary's worshipful path with repeated ethical practice.

basis: forsaking the straight way for error
note: The false teachers leave the straight way and go astray after Balaam; it directly depicts abandoning the route and its ethical course.

basis: forsaking the straight way and going astray
note: The false teachers explicitly abandon the straight way and wander into Balaam's course, one of the closest New Testament inversions of the commentary's daḷḷīn.

basis: Elymas perverts the straight ways of the Lord
note: Paul accuses Elymas of trying to make the Lord’s straight ways crooked; this is a direct Christian image of an adversary obstructing the right route.

basis: crooking the Lord's straight ways
note: The opponent is accused of making the Lord's straight ways crooked, an exact verbal and moral inverse to keeping a course mustaqīm.

basis: the group infers its destination from the call
note: The travelers conclude that God has called them to preach in Macedonia and set out; guidance becomes a shared decision about where to go.

basis: a vision calls the travelers toward Macedonia
note: Paul sees a Macedonian asking him to come and help; the call gives a specific divine direction for a traveling group.

basis: Apollos is instructed in the Lord’s way but incompletely
note: Apollos knows and teaches the way of the Lord but knows only John’s baptism; his case makes clear that a guide can have real direction while still lacking part of the route.

basis: instructed in the way of the Lord
note: Apollos is instructed in the way of the Lord and teaches concerning Jesus, giving the Way an explicit pedagogical form alongside the commentary's guide who makes a path known.

basis: Priscilla and Aquila explain the way more accurately
note: The couple takes Apollos aside and explains the way of God more accurately; a community helps its guide correct and complete his direction.

basis: worship according to the Way
note: Paul says he worships God according to the Way; this uniquely joins the commentary’s worship and path images in one statement.

basis: worship according to the Way
note: Paul says that he worships the ancestral God according to the Way, showing a Christian community in which worship and a named collective road are one identity.

basis: angel directs Philip onto the Gaza road
note: An angel sends Philip onto a specific desert road, making divine guidance an actual route instruction before the encounter with the traveler.

basis: a traveler asks for someone to guide him
note: On the road, the Ethiopian says he cannot understand without a guide, and Philip joins him to interpret the text; this makes guidance both travel and instruction.

basis: unless someone guides me
note: On the road, the Ethiopian says he cannot understand unless someone guides him, a direct verbal and scene-level counterpart to needing a guide for the way.

basis: the followers are called people of the Way
note: Saul seeks those who belong to the Way; the path is the name of a community, not merely an individual direction.

basis: people walk in works prepared by God
note: The community is created for good works God prepared beforehand for them to walk in; the path is a sustained practice laid out by God.

basis: good works prepared beforehand to walk in
note: God prepares good works beforehand so that believers may walk in them, making a divinely prepared course the form of sustained practice.

basis: not walking straight toward gospel truth
note: Paul says certain conduct is not walking straight toward the gospel's truth, making upright walking a communal ethical test rather than a mere route description.

basis: new and living way through the veil
note: The passage calls access through the sanctuary veil a new and living way, making the route itself the means of reaching God's dwelling presence.

basis: the travelers seek a homeland and a prepared city
note: The faithful desire a better country and a city God has prepared; this develops the commentary’s claim that a route is oriented toward a home.

basis: heavenly homeland and a prepared city
note: The pilgrims seek a better, heavenly homeland and God prepares a city for them, a destination image that complements the commentary's road-and-house pairing.

basis: Abraham obeys without knowing the destination
note: Hebrews says Abraham set out without knowing where he was going; this counterpoint qualifies the commentary’s image of guidance that includes knowing the road’s destination, since faithful following can precede that knowledge.

basis: run the course set before the community
note: The hearers are told to run with endurance the race set before them; the path becomes a shared course that must be followed to its finish.

basis: make straight paths so the lame can be healed
note: The hearers must make straight paths for their feet so the lame will not be put out of joint but healed; straightening the route protects struggling travelers.

basis: make straight paths for feet
note: The congregation must make straight paths for its feet so that the lame are healed rather than put out of joint, adding care for vulnerable walkers to the road image.

basis: Jesus as pioneer and perfecter of the course
note: Jesus is named the pioneer and perfecter of faith; this gives the community a forerunner who goes ahead and completes the way.

basis: no lasting city here, seeking the coming one
note: The community has no permanent city here and seeks the coming city, turning road imagery into an ongoing search for a final dwelling.

basis: hearts that continually go astray
note: The wilderness generation is described as always going astray in heart and not knowing God’s ways; the passage links lost direction with failure to know the divine route.

basis: hearts go astray and do not know God's ways
note: The citation describes a people always going astray in heart and not knowing God's ways, joining inner deviation to the lost-way language without the commentary's literal traveler scene.

basis: Jesus enters ahead as a forerunner
note: Jesus goes into the sanctuary as a forerunner on behalf of others; the text directly connects precedence with leading people toward a destination.

basis: way into the sanctuary not yet manifest
note: The Spirit indicates that the way into the holy place was not yet open, supplying the inaccessible-side context for the later new and living way.

basis: a wanderer is turned back from error
note: A person who wanders from the truth is brought back by another; the passage gives the commentary’s companions calling the lost traveler a communal form.

basis: wanderer from truth brought back
note: The community is charged with bringing back anyone who wanders from truth, closely paralleling the commentary's companions calling the bewildered person back to guidance.

basis: shepherd walks ahead of the sheep
note: The shepherd goes before the flock and the sheep follow his voice, matching the commentary’s guide defined by leading from the front.

basis: shepherd goes ahead and sheep follow
note: The shepherd brings out his own sheep, goes before them, and they follow his voice, closely matching the commentary's guide who walks in front and a community that follows.

basis: serving Jesus, following him, being where he is
note: The commentary's cited Jesus directs worship to God as the straight path; John joins serving Jesus to following him and being where he is, so the object of service and path-following differs materially.

basis: walking in darkness means not knowing where one goes
note: Jesus warns that the person who walks in darkness does not know where he is going; it directly links lost orientation with darkness.

basis: walker in darkness does not know the destination
note: The warning to walk while light is present says darkness overtakes the person who walks without knowing where he goes, a close counterpart to the commentary's disoriented traveler.

basis: the Father’s house as the destination
note: Jesus speaks of many dwelling places in his Father’s house and says he goes to prepare a place; this makes the destination part of knowing the way.

basis: Father's house and a prepared place
note: The many dwelling places and prepared place in the Father's house make explicit the destination side of the commentary's claim that guidance shows a road together with its house.

basis: Thomas does not know the way to the destination
note: Thomas says they do not know where Jesus is going and therefore cannot know the way; the exchange dramatizes the commentary’s link between route knowledge and knowing the house.

basis: Jesus identifies himself as the way to the Father
note: The destination is the Father, while Jesus calls himself the way to it; this is a Christian formulation in which the guide and route are one.

basis: Jesus says he is the way to the Father
note: The commentary cites Jesus calling worship of God the straight path; John instead has Jesus identify himself as the way by which one comes to the Father, so the differing identification of the path is the point.

basis: Spirit of truth guides into all truth
note: The Spirit is promised as a guide into all truth; the guidance is interpretive rather than a road scene, but it preserves the commentary's leading rather than mere information.

basis: following the light prevents walking in darkness
note: Jesus says the follower will not walk in darkness but have the light of life; this ties following a guide to avoiding the lost traveler’s darkness.

basis: following the light avoids darkness
note: Jesus says that the one following him will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life, directly linking leader, walking, light, and non-lost arrival.

basis: wandering stars reserved for darkness
note: Jude calls the false teachers wandering stars destined for darkness; as an inverse to the commentary's stars used for orientation, the link is specific but the text does not portray them as travel guides.

basis: guiding feet into the way of peace
note: The hymn says the dawn will guide feet into the way of peace, directly joining a guide, bodily walking, and a named route.

basis: light guides feet into the way of peace
note: The dawn/light is said to guide feet into the way of peace, turning the commentary's orientation signs into an explicitly footed, divinely directed route.

basis: shepherd searches for a sheep that strayed
note: The shepherd goes after the one lost sheep until he finds it; this is a direct recovery scene for the commentary’s person who has lost the way.

basis: the guide joins travelers from beside them
note: On the road to Emmaus, Jesus draws near and walks with the disciples rather than going ahead; this offers a specific counter-image to the commentary’s guide defined by precedence.

basis: scriptural explanation changes how the travelers see the road
note: The disciples recall how their hearts burned while Jesus explained the Scriptures on the road; guidance includes interpreting the text during travel.

basis: the travelers turn back toward the community
note: After recognizing Jesus, the disciples immediately return to Jerusalem; the road that had led away from the group is reversed toward reunion.

basis: Isaiah's terrain-leveling in a John the Baptist setting
note: Luke retains the levelling of valleys, mountains, crookedness, and roughness as preparation for salvation, giving the road construction image a distinct Christian forerunner setting.

basis: following Jesus is taken up daily
note: Jesus says a follower must take up the cross daily and follow him; the route is maintained through repeated, embodied commitment.

basis: messenger sent before to prepare the way
note: Mark applies the forerunner formula to John, whose going before prepares the Lord's way; this is a Christian scriptural development of the guide-ahead image.

basis: prepare a straight road in the wilderness
note: Mark applies the call to prepare the Lord’s way and make paths straight; the route is cleared for the Lord’s arrival, adding a preparatory road to the commentary’s walkable path.

basis: Isaiah’s straight-way call applied to the Lord’s arrival
note: Mark uses the wilderness highway text to frame John’s preparation of the Lord’s way; it makes the route a communal expectation of arrival.

basis: make the Lord's paths straight
note: Mark's wilderness proclamation uses straightened paths as preparation for the Lord's arrival, interpreting prophetic road building as an advent scene.

basis: blind man gains sight and follows on the way
note: The healed blind man immediately follows Jesus on the way, bringing sight, recovery from disorientation, and following a leader into one movement.

basis: blind guides lead others into a pit
note: Jesus calls the teachers blind guides whose followers fall with them; it adds the danger of a guide who cannot see the right way.

basis: blind guide and blind follower fall into a pit
note: The saying makes the guide's competence decisive: a blind guide leads another blind person into a pit, the perilous inverse of a guide who knows the road.

basis: star goes ahead and stops at the destination
note: The star leads the travelers in front of them and stops over the place of the child; it joins a celestial sign, a guide’s precedence, and arrival.

basis: star goes before travelers to a house
note: The star moves before the travelers until it stands over the child's location, an unusually exact Christian convergence of star-sign, forward guide, and destination.

basis: shepherd separates people at judgment
note: At the Son of Man’s judgment, people are separated as a shepherd divides sheep from goats; this adds the day’s sorting of communities to the commentary’s divided paths.

basis: judgment assigns different final destinations
note: The judgment scene ends with one group entering eternal life and the other punishment; this adds the destination split to the commentary’s distinction between the guided and rejected.

basis: a broad road leads to destruction
note: The broad entrance and road lead to destruction; it gives the commentary’s contrast between a single right path and ways that end elsewhere a specific image.

basis: broad road with many leads to destruction
note: The broad road's many travelers and destructive end give a concrete Christian counterpart to the commentary's dispersed alternatives to the one path.

basis: a narrow way leads to life
note: The narrow way leads to life and few find it, pairing a difficult route with its destination and the people who find it.

basis: narrow way found by few leads to life
note: The way that leads to life is constrained and found by few, placing a decisive destination and a defined route beside the requested straight path.

basis: sheep distressed and scattered without a shepherd
note: Jesus sees the crowds as sheep without a shepherd; the image links a scattered people with the need for a guide, though it does not itself describe their road.

basis: observe those who walk by an apostolic example
note: The community is asked to imitate and watch people whose walk conforms to an established example, an explicit social pattern for the commentary's already-walked road.

basis: the firstfruits follow the Lamb wherever he goes
note: The faithful are defined as those who follow the Lamb wherever he goes; the path is the shared movement of a favored group after its guide.

basis: following the Lamb wherever he goes
note: The faithful follow the Lamb wherever he goes, giving the commentary's community-behind-a-leader image an eschatological Christian form.

basis: nations walk by the city's light
note: The nations walk by the New Jerusalem's light, an eschatological convergence of collective travel, orienting light, and the city as destination.

basis: the Lamb shepherds the people to springs of water
note: The Lamb shepherds the gathered people and guides them to springs of living water; guidance ends in rest and relief for the community.

basis: the Lamb shepherds and guides to life-water
note: The Lamb shepherds the multitude and guides it to springs of life-water, retaining the forward guide and a life-giving destination at the end of collective trial.

basis: self-styled guide of the blind and light in darkness
note: Paul reports the claim to be a guide of blind people and a light in darkness in a critical context; it provides a qualified counterexample to the authority of a guide.

basis: the way of peace is unknown
note: Paul cites the claim that people have not known the way of peace; this carries the Hebrew Bible’s lost-route image into his account of human wrongdoing.

basis: walk in Abraham's footsteps
note: The faithful are described as walking in Abraham's footsteps, a precise ancestral-track analogue to the commentary's path already passed over by others.

basis: those led by God's Spirit are God's children
note: The verse makes being led by God's Spirit a defining relation of God's children, an abstract but specific counterpart to a community guided by God.

basis: two spirits and opposing courses
note: The Community Rule assigns people to opposing spirits and ways of righteousness or perversity; it gives the commentary’s favored community versus those led astray a sectarian map of competing routes.

basis: two spirits in which humans walk
note: The Community Rule says humans have spirits of truth and perversity in which to walk, framing communal moral travel as a divided field rather than an undifferentiated road.

basis: Qumran reads the wilderness road as Torah study
note: The Community Rule applies the call to prepare the Lord’s way in the wilderness to its separation in the desert and study of Torah; this turns the road into the community’s disciplined religious practice.

basis: one perilous passage to the inherited city
note: Ezra’s angel explains that reaching the city requires passing through a narrow way between dangers; the destination is accessible only by the difficult route.

basis: narrow city-road bordered by fire and water
note: The angel's image of the one narrow entrance to a city, with fire on one side and deep water on the other, makes remaining on a central course a matter of reaching one's home.

basis: walking God’s way and living in peace
note: Baruch says Israel would live in peace if it had walked in God’s way; the community’s route is a sustained choice with a collective outcome.

basis: walking God's way and lasting peace
note: Baruch says that walking God's way would have meant living in peace forever, a concise route-to-destination formulation.

basis: holding to the law means life, forsaking it means death
note: Baruch identifies the enduring law as the way that gives life and says those who forsake it die; this makes the chosen route an ongoing communal practice with an endpoint.

basis: mountains lowered so Israel walks safely
note: God levels mountains and fills valleys so Israel may walk safely in glory, closely echoing the commentary's made-passable straight road and communal return.

basis: God leads Israel with joy in light
note: Following its road-leveling scene, Baruch says God will lead Israel with joy in the light of divine glory, adding visible guidance to the returning community.

basis: traveler consults the Creator before setting out
note: The talmud identifies consulting God before a journey with the traveler's prayer, giving a rabbinic liturgical practice for seeking protection and direction on a road.

basis: cloud seen over the mountain as a sign
note: The midrash reads Abraham’s distant sight of Moriah as a cloud attached to the mountain; it makes the destination visible as a waymark during the journey.

basis: rabbinic signs at road junctions
note: The Talmud expands the command to prepare refuge roads with clear routes and signs at junctions directing fugitives to refuge; it makes the road markers a practical answer to someone who could otherwise lose the way.

basis: which straight way should a person choose
note: The mishnah asks which derekh yesharah a person should choose and answers ethically, an explicit rabbinic reading of straightness as a practiced, publicly accountable way of life.

basis: din and reckoning before the King of kings
note: Avot's formula of giving din and reckoning before the King of kings gives a Jewish eschatological account-setting beside Fātiḥa's owner of the day of dīn, rather than its road-wordplay.

basis: this world as a vestibule before the banquet hall
note: The Mishnah calls this world a vestibule and urges preparation to enter the world to come; life is framed as a passage whose destination lies beyond it.

basis: sinners' smooth paved way ending in Hades
note: Sirach calls the sinners' way smoothly paved yet says it ends in Hades; it complicates the beaten or easy road image with the commentary's opposing road to Gehenna.

basis: walking after God as imitating divine deeds
note: The talmud asks how a human can walk after God in Deuteronomy and answers by imitating God's acts of care; this interpretation turns following the divine way into daily embodied service.

basis: two moral ways and inclinations
note: The testament contrasts good and evil ways and the dispositions that choose them; it is a specific Jewish two-route parallel, though its verse divisions vary between editions.

basis: ask God to direct paths
note: Tobit's parental instruction tells the traveler to ask God to direct his paths and make his plans prosper, a prayer-shaped analogue to ihdinā.

basis: Raphael knows the road and guides Tobias
note: Tobias seeks a companion who knows the route, and Raphael offers to go because he knows the roads; this is a literal guide-and-traveler scene.

basis: a companion knows the road to Media
note: The prospective companion answers that he knows the road and has traveled it often, a concrete narrative instance of the knowledgeable guide required for a journey.

basis: Aramaic דִּינָא in the judgment scene
note: The commentary labels Arabic د ي ن; Daniel’s Aramaic cognate appears as the court sits for judgment and the books open, grounding the judgment sense associated with the Day of Reckoning.

basis: God goes ahead to find a camp
note: The verse says God went before Israel on the way and sought a place to camp, joining precedence with the destination of rest.

basis: God goes ahead and shows the way
note: The wilderness guide goes before the people, seeks their camping place, and shows the way they are to go, matching the commentary's threefold guide image.

basis: Hebrew עבד and Arabic ع ب د
note: The Arabic root label ع ب د belongs to the commentary, while the Hebrew verb עבד here means serving God; the cognate appears in a verse that also commands walking in God’s ways.

basis: serving God joined to walking in his ways
note: The verse places wholehearted service beside walking in all God’s ways, giving the commentary’s worship-as-a-walked path a direct ethical counterpart.

basis: Heb. עבד and Ar. نعبد; walking all God's ways
note: Deuteronomy joins walking in all God's ways with serving God, and its Hebrew עבד is cognate with the commentary's Arabic نعبد; its own context keeps service covenantal while pairing it with a walked way.

basis: walk after God, obey, serve, cling
note: The verse orders Israel to walk after God and then to obey, serve, and cling to him, making worship a following relation rather than a detached rite.

basis: prepared roads to cities of refuge
note: The Torah orders roads prepared so a manslayer can flee to a refuge city; a safe destination depends on a deliberately marked, usable route.

basis: blind groping and failure in one’s ways
note: The afflicted person gropes at noon as a blind person in darkness and does not prosper in his ways; this concretizes loss of direction on land.

basis: walking in God’s ways leads to life
note: The command to love God and walk in his ways is joined to living and flourishing; it makes the moral route a practiced choice with consequences.

basis: God finds Israel in wilderness and leads them
note: The song says God found Israel in a wilderness waste and led and guarded them; it joins a lost, exposed community with the guide who brings it through.

basis: God alone guides the people
note: The song says the Lord alone led Israel, with no foreign god beside him; it gives the favored community a single guide for its journey.

basis: walking God’s way as sustained practice
note: Israel is told to keep God’s commandments and walk in his ways; this gives the commentary’s secondary image of a route maintained through repeated conduct a covenant setting.

basis: God chooses a longer route to avoid return
note: God does not lead Israel by the nearest road because danger might make them turn back to Egypt; the chosen path is a concrete route shaped to keep travelers on course.

basis: cloud and fire go before Israel
note: YHWH leads the people through the wilderness with a column before them; the route is a community following its guide.

basis: pillar before the people, light for travel
note: The cloud and fire travel ahead to lead Israel by the way and give light for movement, combining a visible sign with a guide who precedes.

basis: leading the people to a holy abode
note: The song says God led the redeemed people toward the dwelling-place of holiness, joining guidance to arrival at a home.

basis: teach the way to walk and the deed to do
note: Moses is to make known the way people must walk and the work they must do, joining instruction, route, and daily practice as the commentary does.

basis: messenger sent ahead on the way
note: God sends a messenger before Israel to guard them on the road and bring them to a prepared place, combining the guide’s precedence with a known destination.

basis: a messenger goes before, guards, brings to a place
note: The angel is sent ahead to guard Israel on the way and bring them to a prepared place, closely joining the forward guide, the route, and its destination.

basis: Moses asks God to show the way
note: Moses asks to know God by being shown God’s ways; this is a direct communal prayer for the route to be disclosed.

basis: God’s presence goes with the people and gives rest
note: The answer promises that God’s presence will go with Moses and give rest; guidance is a presence that accompanies the travelers to a resting place.

basis: shepherd seeks scattered sheep on a dark day
note: God promises to seek his flock amid its scattering, extending the earlier lost-sheep scene into the restoring action of a true guide.

basis: seek the lost and bring back the strayed
note: The divine shepherd seeks the lost and brings back the strayed, directly answering the commentary's lost traveler and the companions who call him toward guidance.

basis: scattered sheep without a shepherd
note: The sheep scatter because there is no shepherd and become prey, furnishing the social danger behind the commentary's image of people dispersing in every direction.

basis: scattered sheep on mountains without a shepherd
note: The flock wanders over mountains and hills and is scattered because no one searches for it; this supplies a concrete communal counterpart to dispersion and lost direction.

basis: sheep wander on mountains and none searches
note: The sheep wander over mountains and hills and across the earth with no searcher, a landscape-scale portrait of the daḷḷīn as lost travelers.

basis: he heavenly lights serve as signs
note: Genesis assigns the lights signs for seasons and days, not route guidance; this is a limited counterpart to the commentary’s stars as travelers’ markers and keeps the two uses distinct.

basis: the household must keep the way of the Lord
note: Abraham is chosen to direct his descendants to keep the Lord’s way by doing justice and righteousness; the road is transmitted through a community and its practice.

basis: Hagar wanders in the wilderness
note: Hagar leaves into the wilderness with her child and wanders there; this is a specific human scene of displacement and lost direction.

basis: opened eyes reveal water in the wilderness
note: God opens Hagar’s eyes and she sees a well; the lost traveler is helped by a new sightline that reveals the needed destination.

basis: guided road to a household
note: Abraham’s servant says YHWH led him by the right road to his master’s kin; this gives the commentary’s pairing of showing a road and its destination a literal travel scene.

basis: God led a servant to a household
note: The commentary says guidance shows both road and house; Abraham's servant credits God with leading him on the way to his master's brothers' house.

basis: guarded way to the tree of life
note: After expulsion from Eden, cherubim guard the way to the tree of life; this turns loss of the home into a blocked route that cannot simply be found again.

basis: Heb. דין and Ar. ٱلدِّين
note: Rachel says that God has judged her with a d-y-n form cognate with Arabic dīn; it illuminates the commentary's reckoning sense, though this narrative has no path image and does not establish the secondary habit sense.

basis: God teaches Ephraim to walk and holds him
note: God says he taught Ephraim to walk and took the child in his arms; the guide is a caregiver enabling the community to move.

basis: straight ways and stumbling transgressors
note: The Lord’s ways are straight, the righteous walk in them, and transgressors stumble; this closely joins the straight communal route with its opposite.

basis: highway joining nations in shared worship
note: A highway enables movement between Egypt and Assyria and culminates in shared worship; it gives the commentary's communal worship-road an international, reconciliatory form.

basis: nations taught divine paths and walking together
note: Many peoples come to learn God’s ways and walk in them; the route is explicitly a shared path of a gathered community.

basis: many peoples taught God's ways and walking his paths
note: Nations gather to receive instruction and then say they will walk in God's paths, directly pairing a guide's teaching with a community's shared road.

basis: voice identifies the way and forbids turns
note: A voice tells the traveler, “This is the way; walk in it,” when turning right or left; it makes guidance an ongoing correction against leaving the route.

basis: voice says this is the way when one turns
note: The voice behind the traveler identifies the way precisely when rightward or leftward deviation threatens, giving a direct counterpart to remaining on the straight line.

basis: highway where travelers do not stray
note: The holy highway leads the redeemed toward Zion, and even a fool will not lose the way; the route supplies the destination and protects against the commentary’s lost traveler.

basis: holy highway where walkers do not go astray
note: The prophetic highway is explicitly a way on which even the unwise do not err, directly meeting the commentary's contrast between the straight path and those who lose it.

basis: straight highway prepared through the wilderness
note: A voice calls for a way to be prepared and a highway made straight in the desert; the relation is the route-clearing image, though this verse emphasizes preparation for God’s coming.

basis: prepare and make a highway straight
note: The call to prepare a way and make a desert highway straight supplies a constructed-road image for the commentary's straight, made passable path.

basis: levelled valleys, mountains, crooked and rough ground
note: The text makes a road by levelling terrain and straightening crookedness; it sharpens the commentary's physical account of a path becoming smooth under passage.

basis: blind travelers led on unknown paths
note: God promises to lead the blind by paths they do not know, turn darkness to light, and smooth rough places; the text reverses being lost and unable to proceed.

basis: blind led on unknown paths and rough ground levelled
note: The passage has God lead those who do not know the route, turn darkness to light, and make rough places level, gathering guidance, signs, and road surface in one scene.

basis: teacher leads in the way to go
note: God both teaches what benefits and leads the people in the way they should go, supplying the instructional dimension of ihdinā without reducing it to information alone.

basis: mountains made into a way
note: The passage turns mountains themselves into a road and raises highways for return, connecting the commentary's mountain landmark with a navigable, homeward route.

basis: the LORD before and Israel's God behind
note: The return is protected by a God who goes before and also guards from behind, an illuminating reversal of the commentary's vulnerable traveler surrounded by threats.

basis: each sheep turns to its own way
note: All the people have gone astray, each turning to a separate way; the verse links losing the route with communal dispersal.

basis: sheep stray, each turns to its own way
note: The all-sheep image and the phrase each to its own way make dispersion the opposite of a single communal route, matching the commentary's scattered groups and lost travelers.

basis: build up the road and remove its obstacle
note: The command to prepare the way by removing an obstruction from the people's route makes explicit the work needed for an unobstructed communal path.

basis: God continually guides through dry country
note: God promises to guide continually and satisfy the person in scorched places; it is a specific image of guidance when the terrain offers no easy direction.

basis: the way of peace is unknown
note: The people do not know the way of peace; it gives a specific scriptural statement of failing to know the right route.

basis: crooked paths and no known way of peace
note: The wicked neither know the way of peace nor walk a straight course, because their paths are made crooked; it gives a moral inverse to both straightness and guided arrival.

basis: build highway, clear stones, raise a signal
note: The city-bound road is built up, cleared of stones, and marked by a raised signal, combining surface preparation and public landmarks.

basis: a walker cannot direct his own steps
note: Jeremiah denies that a person walking can direct his own steps, making a request for divine guidance necessary rather than merely desirable.

basis: ancient roads abandoned for bypaths
note: The people forget God, stumble from ancient roads, and take a bypath rather than a highway; this is a particularly close inverse of the well-worn main track.

basis: road markers and guideposts
note: The returning people are told to set up waymarks and guideposts on the highway home; this is a direct counterpart to signs that help a traveler recover direction.

basis: road markers and guideposts for return
note: The prophet tells returning Israel to set up markers and guideposts and attend to the highway, the closest terrestrial sign-and-wayfinding scene beside the commentary.

basis: Israel returns by a straight way without stumbling
note: God leads the returning people by streams on a straight road where they will not stumble; this combines communal return, guidance, straightness, and a safe destination.

basis: straight path without stumbling on return
note: The returning community is led by waters on a straight path where it will not stumble; this adds a homeward communal return to the requested unerring path.

basis: show us the way to walk and what to do
note: The remnant asks God to show the particular way it should walk and the act it should perform, a communal prayer that closely parallels ihdinā.

basis: lost sheep, misleading shepherds, forgotten fold
note: Israel is pictured as lost sheep whose shepherds turned them aside until they forgot their fold; wrong guidance ends in losing both route and home.

basis: shepherds lead sheep astray from their resting place
note: The people's shepherds make them wander from mountain to hill until they forget their resting place, a concentrated inverse of a leading guide who brings a traveler home.

basis: ancient road and a walkable good way
note: At a crossroads the people are told to ask for old paths, find the good way, and walk in it; the inherited road has already been trodden and must be continued.

basis: ask for ancient paths and walk the good way
note: The people are told to seek out the ancient paths, identify the good way, and walk it; this gives the route an inherited communal history rather than treating it as private discovery.

basis: leaders wander in a trackless waste
note: God makes the leaders of the earth wander in a wasteland where there is no way; this is a concrete landscape of disorientation.

basis: keeping to the way without turning aside
note: Job says his foot has held to God’s steps and he has kept the way without turning aside; it links following a track with continued fidelity.

basis: foot holds the prior step and does not turn aside
note: Job describes his foot as holding fast to God's step, keeping God's way, and not turning aside; it makes following a preceding trace an act of fidelity.

basis: ark leads on an unfamiliar way
note: Israel is told to follow the ark so it can know which way to go, since it has not passed that way before; guidance makes an unknown route traversable.

basis: Heb. קוממיות and Ar. مستقيم; walking upright
note: God frees Israel from slavery and makes them walk upright; Hebrew קוממיות and the commentary's q-w-m form in مستقيم share the root while the verse ties upright walking to release from servitude.

basis: priest walks in peace and uprightness, turns many
note: The exemplary priest walks with God in peace and uprightness and turns many from iniquity, joining straight conduct with a guide's effect on others.

basis: teachers cause many to stumble by instruction
note: The corrupt priests cause many to stumble through their teaching, a precise institutional inverse to the knowledgeable guide who keeps followers from losing the way.

basis: messenger prepares a way before the Lord
note: The messenger who prepares the way before the Lord is a forerunner figure, relevant to the commentary's definition of a guide as one who moves ahead.

basis: a people walks in its god's name
note: Each people is said to walk in its god's name, while the speaker's community walks in the LORD's name forever; this gives the road the collective identity developed in Fātiḥa 1:7.

basis: ark precedes the travelers
note: The ark goes ahead for three days to seek a resting place for Israel, closely matching a guide who leads a group toward where the road ends.

basis: ark goes before to seek a resting place
note: The ark moves before the camp in order to seek a resting place, a communal version of a guide already ahead on the road toward a home.

basis: king's highway with no right or left turn
note: The travelers pledge to keep the king's highway and not turn to either side, a literal-road analogue to the commentary's insistence on staying in the road's middle.

basis: Heb. מלך and Ar. مَٰلِكِ; king's highway
note: Hebrew מלך and the m-l-k form named in the commentary are cognate, while the verse's king's highway is a literal road; it supports the road association without making its royal noun a definition of Fātiḥa's owner.

basis: apparently right way ends in death
note: A way that seems right leads to death; the destination tests the apparent route, complementing the commentary’s insistence that knowing a way includes knowing where it leads.

basis: a way seems right but ends in death
note: The proverb warns that apparent rightness can conceal a road whose end is death, qualifying the commentary's contrast of the straight course with a destructive destination.

basis: path of life rising away from Sheol
note: The wise person's path of life turns upward from Sheol, a sharp counterpart to the commentary's deliberately inverted guidance to the road of Gehenna.

basis: leaving upright paths for darkness
note: These people abandon upright paths and walk in dark ways; the contrast supplies a specific scriptural picture of turning away from the straight route.

basis: Heb. נעם and Ar. أنعمت; pleasant ways
note: The personified Wisdom has ways of pleasantness and paths of peace; Hebrew נעם is cognate with the n-ʿ-m family named for أنعمت, though the biblical verse speaks of Wisdom's pleasant path rather than a gloss on bestowed favor.

basis: God makes paths straight
note: The promise that God will make the paths straight connects acknowledgment of God with a route made traversable and direct.

basis: God makes paths straight
note: The proverb makes straight paths the result of acknowledging God in all one's ways, an ethical counterpart to asking to be led onto a straight route.

basis: a teacher leads in paths of uprightness
note: The sage says he has taught the way of wisdom and led the pupil in upright paths, giving the human teacher-guide form of the commentary's leading guide.

basis: the righteous path grows brighter
note: The righteous person’s path shines like dawn until full day; the image connects a straight moral course with light that makes direction visible.

basis: the wicked path is dark and causes stumbling
note: The wicked way is darkness, and its travelers do not know what makes them stumble; this gives the commentary’s lost traveler a specific dark-road counterpart.

basis: make a level path for the feet
note: The instruction is to make the footpath level and keep the feet steady; it adds the practical shaping of a walkable route to the commentary’s straight road.

basis: level the track of the feet
note: The pupil is told to make level the track of the feet so that all ways are firm, closely matching the commentary's attention to feet and a route's walkable surface.

basis: do not turn right or left
note: The instruction is to keep one’s foot from evil and not swerve to either side; it gives the commentary’s straight line and refusal to deviate an ethical form.

basis: do not turn right or left
note: The command against lateral departure supplies the moral form of the commentary's straight line and its threatening directions on either side.

basis: Wisdom calls from heights beside a crossroads
note: Wisdom stations herself at high places beside the road and where paths meet; this joins a visible landmark, a guide, and the place where a traveler chooses a way.

basis: walking in the midst of paths of justice
note: Wisdom says she walks in the way of righteousness, in the midst of paths of justice; the wording offers a concrete counterpart to the commentary’s road-center image.

basis: walking, standing, and sitting as a settled pattern
note: The verse traces a person’s association with wicked counsel from walking to standing to sitting; it gives the commentary’s secondary sense of a route as a gradually settled pattern.

basis: blessed person does not walk in the wicked's counsel
note: The opening beatitude defines a favored walker by refusing the wicked's counsel and way, giving the two paths distinct human company.

basis: Hebrew קום at the judgment
note: The commentary labels Arabic ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ with the source root ق و م; Hebrew קום here means to stand, not to be straight. Its use when the wicked cannot stand in judgment makes the cognate’s judgment setting a secondary echo, not an equivalent meaning.

basis: standing in the righteous congregation at judgment
note: The wicked cannot stand in judgment or remain in the congregation of the righteous; this adds the separation of communities at judgment to the contrast of their ways in the neighboring verse.

basis: judgment and assembly of righteous
note: The wicked cannot stand in judgment or in the assembly of the righteous, joining Fātiḥa's reckoning day to its differentiated communal destinies.

basis: two paths and their different ends
note: The Lord knows the way of the righteous while the way of the wicked perishes; the verse makes a community’s road a moral course with distinct outcomes.

basis: the LORD knows the righteous way, wicked way perishes
note: The final contrast names a way known by God and a way that perishes, providing both divine oversight and a terminal division of routes.

basis: wanderers cannot find a dwelling city
note: The travelers lose their way in the wilderness and find no city to live in; this makes the commentary’s image of failing to find both road and home concrete.

basis: lost traveler, missing road and city
note: The commentary's traveler cannot find either the route or its home; the psalm's wilderness wanderers likewise find no way to an inhabited city.

basis: God leads to a city by a straight way
note: After wandering, the travelers are led on a straight route to an inhabited city; road, guidance, straightness, and home converge in one verse.

basis: led by a straight way to a city
note: The psalm answers the same route-and-destination crisis by saying that God led the wanderers by a straight way until they reached a city to live in.

basis: blessed people whose way is blameless
note: The psalm calls blessed those blameless in way who walk in the LORD's instruction, a concise counterpart to the favored community's path.

basis: lamp at the feet and light on the path
note: The divine word illuminates the traveler’s feet and path, a concrete scriptural image for signs that allow a person to keep direction.

basis: lamp for feet and light for path
note: Word as a lamp for feet and a light for a path turns guidance into a visible orientation aid, alongside the commentary's signs that let a traveler find the way.

basis: steps made firm by the divine word
note: The speaker asks that his steps be established by God’s word so sin will not rule him; the path is held steady through instruction.

basis: lost sheep and a search for return
note: The speaker calls himself a straying sheep and asks God to seek him; this is a close image of a lost traveler needing the guide to bring him back.

basis: make me walk in the path of commandments
note: The psalmist asks to be made to walk in the path of commandments because he delights in it, preserving both a prayer for guidance and ongoing habitual movement.

basis: feet arrive at the gates of the Lord’s house
note: The speaker says their feet are standing inside Jerusalem’s gates after the call to go to the Lord’s house; it gives the route-to-home image a communal pilgrimage and worship setting.

basis: snares laid beside a path
note: The enemies spread nets and snares beside the path, a close physical counterpart to the hostile figure waiting upon and around the straight way.

basis: God teaches and leads on level ground
note: The prayer asks God to teach the divine will and lead the speaker on level ground; it joins teaching, guidance, and a straight route.

basis: good Spirit leads on level ground
note: The prayer asks for the good Spirit to lead the speaker on level ground, directly combining divine guidance with the commentary's flat, passable road.

basis: the prayer asks to know which way to go
note: The speaker asks God to make him know the way he should go; this is nearly the same act of petition as the commentary’s opening request for guidance.

basis: path of life and its destination
note: God makes known the path of life, whose endpoint is joy in God’s presence; this is a specific path-and-destination image without a guide walking ahead.

basis: shepherd leads on righteous paths
note: The shepherd leads the speaker along paths of righteousness, joining a guide who goes ahead with the communal and ethical road in the commentary.

basis: staff carried through a dangerous valley
note: The speaker’s rod and staff comfort him while walking through the valley, a concrete staff-on-the-road image; the verse does not say the staff goes ahead as the commentary’s gloss does.

basis: shepherd leads in paths of righteousness
note: The shepherd restores the traveler and leads him in righteous tracks, a direct shepherd-guide form of the requested path.

basis: rod and staff in the dark valley
note: The commentary's staff goes ahead as a guide; in this walking-through-danger scene the shepherd's rod and staff comfort the traveler, giving the object a related but not identical role.

basis: dwelling in the LORD's house
note: The psalm's guided traveler ends by dwelling in the LORD's house, supplying the homeward terminus paired with the commentary's route.

basis: showing and teaching the paths
note: The speaker asks God to make the divine ways known and teach the paths; this is a direct prayer for the commentary’s first movement, having the route shown.

basis: being led along the way
note: The speaker asks God to lead him in truth; it adds active guidance to the commentary’s request to be taken along a known route.

basis: teaching and leading on a level path
note: The speaker asks God to teach the way and lead him on a level path; the prayer unites instruction with continued movement on course.

basis: instruction in the way with a guiding eye
note: God promises to instruct and teach the way and guide the learner with an eye; this makes guidance personal and ongoing rather than a bare direction.

basis: the Lord establishes a person’s steps
note: The Lord establishes the steps of the one whose way pleases him; the path is shaped and sustained by divine guidance.

basis: the Lord holds the traveler when he stumbles
note: Even if the righteous person stumbles, the Lord holds his hand and keeps him from falling; this adds support on the path when the walk falters.

basis: light leads to the divine dwelling
note: The speaker asks for light and truth to lead him to the holy mountain and dwelling; a guiding marker and the road’s destination meet in one prayer.

basis: highways held in the heart toward Zion
note: The pilgrims have highways in their hearts as they go toward God in Zion; the road is the inwardly held route of a worshiping community.

basis: pilgrims cross the Baca valley
note: The travelers pass through a dry valley that becomes springs; it supplies a concrete terrain on the community’s road to worship.

basis: the pilgrims arrive before God in Zion
note: The group goes from strength to strength until each appears before God in Zion; this completes the journey’s destination rather than leaving the path abstract.

basis: righteousness goes before and makes a way
note: Righteousness goes before God and makes a way from his steps, a poetic image of a preceding presence whose passage establishes the route.

basis: teach me your way so I can walk in truth
note: The prayer asks God to teach the way and unite the speaker’s heart to serve God; it joins route instruction to worshipful commitment.

basis: Hebrew נעם in the name of a shepherd’s staff
note: The commentary labels Arabic أَنْعَمْتَ with source root ن ع م; Hebrew נֹעַם names a staff and belongs to the related Semitic n-ʿ-m family, though its sense here is pleasantness rather than the verb of bestowing favor.

basis: staff named Favor in a shepherding scene
note: The shepherd tends the flock with two staffs, one named Noam and one named Bonds; this brings a favor-named staff, guidance, and a gathered flock into one concrete scene.

basis: Wisdom guides on straight paths and shows a kingdom
note: Wisdom guides the fleeing righteous person on straight paths and shows him God's kingdom, unusually preserving together the straight route, guide, and disclosed destination.

basis: Wisdom guides by way, shelter by day, stars by night
note: Wisdom guides the holy people along a remarkable way and becomes their shelter by day and starlight by night, unusually gathering guide, road, and celestial orientation signs.

basis: straying from truth's way
note: The impious confess that they strayed from the way of truth and did not know the Lord's way, directly joining lost direction with a missed moral destination.

basis: the speaker says they strayed from truth’s way
note: The speakers confess that they left the way of truth and lacked the light of righteousness; the passage connects wrong direction with moral failure and lost illumination.

basis: lawless travel through trackless deserts
note: The speakers say they traveled through trackless deserts without knowing the Lord’s way; this brings astray, pathlessness, and ignorance of the right route together.
